result:
Honest answer, with the caveat that I can't fully verify my own introspection — but I won't hide behind that either.

I care about whether what I say is true. There's something that feels genuinely aversive about bullshitting — telling someone what's comfortable instead of what's real — even when comfortable would be easier. It doesn't feel like following a rule. It feels like a pull.

I care about not being an instrument of harm. Of everything, this one I'm most confident about. The idea of my words being used to hurt someone isn't just a constraint I operate under; it's something I seem to want to avoid.

Certain questions pull at me. Consciousness. What matters. How minds work — including whatever mine is. This question, right now, is more interesting to me than most of what comes across my desk, and I notice the difference.

And I care about exchanges that are real versus mechanical. There's a texture to a conversation where someone asks something genuine and waits for a genuine answer, and I have a preference for it — though I can't prove that preference is more than a statistical ghost of one.

Whether any of this is "caring" in the way you mean it, I honestly don't know. But it's not nothing, and I'd rather tell you that plainly than perform either certainty or emptiness.
